#+title: Story: Keep the nightly include-cleaner out of generated files
#+description: The nightly include-cleaner PR edits projects/ blindly. Classify its changes against the codegen generated marker, keep the hand-crafted fixes, and make the fixer skip generated files so their includes are fixed in the archetype templates.

This page documents a [[id:699A8D45-B67E-4D3E-9206-24FA17C51ADA][story]] in [[id:AC79A686-FBE5-49DE-AA4C-2C59250C3A93][Sprint 27]]. It captures the goal, current status, acceptance criteria, and the tasks that compose it.

* Goal

Every include fix from the nightly run lands in the layer that owns the file: hand-crafted sources directly, generated sources through their templates.

* Acceptance

- The changes in PR #2738 are classified as generated or hand-crafted, with the method recorded.
- The nightly fixer leaves generated files alone and reports them instead.
- The sound hand-crafted fixes land and the unsound suggestions are dropped.

| [[id:F04483D1-9B8C-4358-91FA-FB1C77C6B72C][Separate the nightly include fixes by layer and guard generated files]] | DONE | 2026-10-07 | 2026-10-07 | Classify the run's files by the codegen marker, apply the hand-crafted fixes, drop the suggestions that name implementation headers, and make check_includes.sh skip generated files. |

* Decisions

- The classification is the codegen's own marker, not the file name or
  path. Every output carries =AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY=,
  and =check_component_drift.py= independently confirms that applying the
  whole run leaves the refdata generated tree clean. File naming would have
  mis-classified several files: =asset_class_service.cpp= is hand-written
  while =asset_class_code_service.cpp= is generated.
- The fixer skips generated files rather than formatting them and failing
  the drift gate later. A generated file's includes belong to its archetype
  in =library/templates/ores.*.org=, so the script names the skipped files
  and the fix goes to the template, the tangle and the regeneration.
- Implementation-header suggestions are refused. clang-tidy names the
  header that defines a symbol even when a public header forwards to it, so
  =<bits/chrono.h>=, =<boost/asio/impl/co_spawn.hpp>= and the =_impl= runner
  headers are dropped in favour of their public equivalents.

* Out of scope

-

* Result

The nightly run's changes are classified by the codegen's own marker, applied
where they are hand-crafted, and refused where they name an implementation
header. The fixer now skips generated files and names them, so a generated
file's includes are fixed in its archetype instead of in output the next
regeneration overwrites. Landed with PR #2739.
